paper.title: Optimality of Thompson Sampling for Gaussian Bandits Depends on Priors

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed stochastic bandit in the normal distribution model with unknown means and variances
settings.definition_quote: We consider the $K$-armed stochastic bandit problem in the normal distribution model. The gambler pulls an arm $i\in\{1,\cdots,K\}$ at each round and receives a reward independently and identically distributed by $\normal(\mu_i,\si_i^2)$... The gambler does not know the parameter $(\mu_i,\si_i^2) \in \mathbb{R}\times (0,\infty)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Two-armed normal bandit with full information on arm 2 known beforehand (lower bound)
unmapped: the learner knows the mean and variance (mu_2, sigma_2^2) of arm 2 exactly
settings.definition_quote: we consider a two-armed setting more advantageous to the gambler in which the full information on the arm 2 is known beforehand, that is, the prior on the arm 2 is the unit point mass measure $\de_{\{(\mu_2,\si_2^2)\}}$

algorithms.name: Thompson Sampling with prior (sigma_i^2)^{-1-alpha} (alpha<0, conservative prior, e.g. uniform prior)
Thompson Sampling with prior (sigma_i^2)^{-1-alpha}, alpha>=0 (reference / Jeffreys prior)

tuning: n_0 = max{2, 3 - ceil(2 alpha)} initial pulls per arm

source.label: thm_possible
source.quote: Let $\ep>0$ be arbitrary and assume that there is a unique optimal arm. Under Thompson sampling with $\al<0$, the expected regret is bounded as \E[\mathrm{Regret}(T)] \le \sum_{i:\De_i>0}\frac{\De_i\log T}{\dmin(\De_i,\si_i^2)}+\lo((\log T)^{4/5}).

results.notes: D_inf(Delta,sigma^2)=(1/2)log(1+Delta^2/sigma^2). Leading term is exact (constant 1), only the remainder is O((log T)^{4/5}); this matches the Burnetas-Katehakis lower bound, so asymptotically optimal. Corollary 7 is the same statement under the normalisation (mu_1,sigma_1^2)=(0,1). Regret defined as sum Delta_{J(t)}, so pseudo-regret.

bound.expression: sum_subopt(Delta_i*(2*log(T)/log(1 + (Delta_i - 2*eps_alg)**2/(sigma_i**2 + eps_alg)) + 2 - 2*alpha_prior + sqrt(sigma_i**2 + eps_alg)/(Delta_i - 2*eps_alg) + 1/(1 - exp(-eps_alg/(2*sigma_i**2))) + 1/(1 - exp(-(eps_alg/sigma_i**2 - log(1 + eps_alg/sigma_i**2))/2)))) + Delta_max*(1/(1 - exp(-eps_alg**2/2)) + 1/(1 - exp(-(1 - log(2))/2)) + beta(1/2, -alpha_prior)/(1 - exp(-eps_alg**2/2))**2 + 2*sqrt(2)/eps_alg*(1 + eps_alg**2/8)**(1 - alpha_prior)/(1 - (1 + eps_alg**2/8)**(-1/2)))

symbols.alpha_prior: prior parameter alpha of the prior (sigma_i^2)^{-1-alpha}, alpha<0

conditions: arm 1 is the unique optimal arm
tuning: eps_alg < min_i Delta_i/2 free analysis parameter

source.label: lem_possible
source.quote: Fix any $\al<0$ and assume that $(\mu_1,\si_1^2)=(0,1)$ and the arm 1 is the unique optimal arm. Then, for any $\ep<\min_{i:\De_i>0}\De_i/2$, \E[\mathrm{Regret}(T)] \le \sum_{i: \De_i>0}\De_i\Bigg( \frac{\log T}{\dmin(\De_i-2\ep,\si_i^2+\ep)}+2-2\al ... \Bigg) + \De_{\max}\Bigg(...\Bigg) = \sum_{i: \De_i>0}\frac{\De_i\log T}{\dmin(\De_i-\ep,\si_i^2+\ep)}+\lo(\ep^{-4})

results.notes: h(x)=(x-1-log x)/2 expanded; h(2)=(1-log 2)/2. The term 1/(1-e^{-eps/(2 sigma_i^2)}) is copied as in the lemma statement though Lemma 10 has eps^2/(2 sigma_i^2) (likely typo); similarly Delta_max term uses eps^2/2 while Lemma 8 has eps^2/8. Recorded as stated in Lemma 6.

conditions: algorithm is Thompson sampling with prior parameter alpha >= 0 on arm 1 and mut_2(t) = mu_2 (arm 2 known)

source.label: thm_impossible
source.quote: Assume that there are $K=2$ arms such that $\mu_1>\mu_2$. Then, under Thompson sampling such that $\mut_1(t)\sim \pi(\mu_1 |\samplen{1}{t})$ with $\al\ge 0$ and $\mut_2(t)=\mu_2$, there exists a constant $\xi>0$ independent of $\si_2$ such that \liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{\E[\regret(T)]}{\log T}\ge \xi.

results.notes: Lower bound for a specific algorithm (TS with reference/Jeffreys-type priors). Since xi is independent of sigma_2 while the optimal constant vanishes as sigma_2->0, TS with alpha>=0 is not asymptotically optimal.

conditions: algorithm is Thompson sampling with prior parameter alpha > 0 on arm 1 (e.g. Jeffreys prior alpha=1/2) and mut_2(t) = mu_2 (arm 2 known)

source.label: thm_impossible
source.quote: In particular, if $\al>0$ then there exist $\xi'>0$ and $\eta>0$ such that \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{\E[\regret(T)]}{T^{\eta}}\ge \xi'.

results.notes: Polynomial expected regret for TS with alpha>0. Paper writes liminf_{N->infty}, interpreted as T->infinity.
